bihar_raw_news.title: Gandak, Kosi river water levels rise in Bihar following Nepal floods - Newsonair
bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 31, 2026 8:58 AM Gandak, Kosi river water levels rise in Bihar following Nepal floods Following severe flooding in Nepal and heavy rainfall in the catchment areas, the water levels in Gandak and Kosi rivers have risen in Bihar. To regulate the river flow, all 36 gates of the Valmikinagar Barrage and 20 gates of the Kosi Barrage have been opened. However, the water levels and discharge of both rivers have declined over the past 24 hours. Meanwhile, amid misleading reports circulating on social media, the Supaul district administration has clarified that the water level of the Kosi River is rising at a normal rate and the Kosi Barrage is completely safe. The situation is being continuously monitored. In view of the possibility of a further rise in water levels, the administrations of West Champaran, East Champaran, Saran and Gopalganj districts have been put on alert.

Bansagar Agreement and River Basin Context The Bansagar Agreement was signed in 1973 by Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and undivided Bihar. The Sone river is a major tributary of the Ganga and supports irrigation in the eastern plains of India. Institutional Mediation and Project Linkages The Union Ministry of Jal Shakti mediated the settlement through a committee chaired by the Central Water Commission (CWC). national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has arrived in Bishkek on a two-day visit to Kyrgyzstan. He was received at the airport by Kasymaliev Adylbek Aleshovich, chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. A traditional Kyrgyz dance performance was also organised to welcome him. Mr Modi is visiting Kyrgyzstan at the invitation of President Sadyr Zhaparov for 26th SCO Summit. On the first day of his visit to Kyrgyzstan, PM Modi will hold bilateral meetings with SCO leaders on the sidelines of the summit. He will also participate in several other programmes. Mr Modi will address the SCO Summit tomorrow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will first interact with the Friends of India in Bishkek today. He will then visit the Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Park and pay floral tributes at the statue of Mahatma Gandhi. The statue was unveiled by Mr Modi during his visit to Kyrgyzstan in the year 2015. The Prime Minister will also hold bilateral meetings with several leaders of SCO member countries today. These include meetings with the Presidents of Armenia, Kyrgyzstan and Iran, as well as a bilateral meeting with the President of Russia. Mr Modi will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games today. The event celebrates the rich and vibrant cultural heritage of Central Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the 26th Summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation tomorrow, the first of September. Vikalp Shukla, Akashvani News, Bishkek.” In his departure statement on Saturday, Mr Modi said he is looking forward to advancing India’s vision for the region, based on “security, connectivity and opportunity”. He also said India will work with SCO members towards a region free from “terrorism, separatism and extremism”. Mr Modi will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games. He said the visit will strengthen India’s strategic partnerships in Central Asia, deepen its civilisational connect with the region and advance the shared pursuit of peace, stability and prosperity. The summit theme is “25 Years of the SCO: Together Towards Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity. The summit’s priorities include counter-terrorism, regional stability and coordination on cross-border threats. The Bishkek Declaration and other summit texts are expected to be finalised during heads-of-state session tomorrow.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | International 39 Death toll in Nepal flash flood rises to 794, while more than 2,500 people still missing
national_raw_news.content: Nepal has intensified efforts to free hundreds of people trapped inside tunnels at hydropower projects, including the Trishuli-3A site, following Wednesday’s flash floods. Rescuers, including experts from India and China have been attempting to make contact but have so far received no response from inside the tunnel. Hundreds of the 2,500 people reported missing are believed to be employees of Nepal’s hydropower projects. Wednesday’s disaster has killed at least 794 people and more than 2,500 people are missing in Nepal. In Tibet, the official death toll is 16, with 546 reported to be missing, while rescuers are struggling to find survivors. Bodies have been recovered from all eight affected districts of Nepal as rescuers race against time to search for those missing and rescue those stranded. A suspension bridge in central Nepal was swept away today due to a fresh flood in the Trishuli River. The bridge connected Ghyalchowk of Gandaki Rural Municipality-8 in Gorkha district of Gandaki province with Charaudi along the Prithvi Highway. The flood, which lasted for around three hours, swept away the bridge at around 11.30 AM. With the flood washing away the bridge, residents of Gandaki Rural Municipality 7 and 8 have lost their access to the Prithvi Highway. Before this, the devastating flash floods on August 26 had swept away a bridge at Dhawadighat, a little distance downstream from Kathmandu. Locals had been using the Ghyalchowk-Charaudi Bridge as an alternative to the Dhawadighat Bridge.

national_raw_news.title: Odisha likely to receive extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places today 20 mins ago 10
national_raw_news.content: Odisha faces another spell of heavy to very heavy rain today, with the weather system over the northwest Bay of Bengal continuing to influence the state. The IMD has forecast extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places today, with a red warning in force for Bargarh and orange warnings for several districts of western Odisha. The fresh spell comes when parts of Kendrapara, Bhadrak and Jajpur are still recovering from the recent floods, raising concerns of renewed inundation in vulnerable areas. Odisha is facing another spell of heavy rain today, as a well-marked low-pressure area over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining West Bengal-North Odisha coast continues to influence the state. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall at several places, with extremely heavy rain at isolated places. For today, a red warning has been issued for Bargarh, while Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Sambalpur, Deogarh, Angul, Keonjhar, Subarnapur, Nuapada, Balangir and Kalahandi are under orange warning. The IMD says the system is likely to move west-northwestwards across north Odisha and Gangetic West Bengal during the next 24 hours. The renewed rain comes as more than sixty-seven thousand people were still affected by the recent floods in Kendrapara, Bhadrak and Jajpur. The IMD has warned that heavy rainfall could lead to localised flooding, waterlogging and riverine flooding in vulnerable catchments.

Last month, a high-level coordination meeting was conducted under the chairmanship of the Hon’ble Chief Secretary, Himachal Pradesh , to facilitate coordinated action for timely implementation of NBM 2.0 and other telecom initiatives. Under NBM 2.0 , emphasis is being laid on expanding Optical Fibre Cable (OFC) and broadband connectivity in rural, remote, hilly, border and uncovered areas, including connectivity to schools, PHCs, Anganwadi Centres and Panchayat offices . The joint efforts are also focused on expediting BharatNet, 4G Saturation and other Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN)-funded telecom projects . Special attention is being given to resolving bottlenecks relating to Right of Way (RoW), land allotment, electricity connections and OFC laying/restoration , particularly in difficult terrain. DoT and the State Government are working closely with BSNL, Telecom Service Providers and infrastructure stakeholders to address operational challenges and ensure timely project implementation. These initiatives will strengthen reliable, resilient and inclusive digital connectivity across Himachal Pradesh and further advance the vision of Digital India , ensuring better access to digital services for citizens, particularly in remote and underserved areas. national_raw_news.content: Commerce Secretary co-chairs India-Brazil 8th Trade Monitoring Mechanism meeting; Commits early finalisation and greater market access for Indian pharmaceuticals Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Commerce Secretary co-chairs India-Brazil 8th Trade Monitoring Mechanism meeting; Commits early finalisation and greater market access for Indian pharmaceuticals ANI | Updated: Aug 31, 2026 10:59 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Brasilia [Brazil], August 31 (ANI): Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal co-chaired the India-Brazil 8th Trade Monitoring Mechanism (TMM) meeting in Brasilia, where India and Brazil committed to early finalisation of key trade terms and greater market access for Indian pharmaceuticals , according to the Ministry of Commerce & Industry. Co-chaired alongside Brazil's Secretary of Foreign Trade, Tatiana Lacerda Prazeres, the meeting reviewed bilateral trade performance, which reached USD 15.07 billion in 2025-26. Both nations reaffirmed their target to expand trade to USD 30 billion by 2030, identifying pharmaceuticals, chemicals, engineering goods, and machinery as core areas for diversification. Agrawal also held talks with Brazil's Minister of Development, Industry, Commerce and Services, Marcio Elias Rosa, to explore deeper investment cooperation. Both delegations reviewed progress on the India-MERCOSUR Terms of Reference to expand and modernise the existing Preferential Trade Agreement, following bilateral trade with the MERCOSUR bloc reaching USD 20.84 billion in 2025. Both sides committed to an early conclusion of these terms. Discussions placed specific emphasis on pharmaceutical trade facilitation, anchored by the CDSCO-ANVISA memorandum of understanding signed in February 2026. The Indian delegation noted that the framework provides an institutional base to improve market entry. "India emphasised the need for supporting more predictable regulatory pathways and facilitating greater market access," the Ministry noted, highlighting that "India can contribute to the availability of affordable, quality medicines and strengthen efforts towards more accessible healthcare." In agriculture, the discussions advanced technical evaluations regarding priority phytosanitary requests to enable reciprocal concessions within a fixed timeframe. The two sides noted progress on mutual recognition of Electronic Certificates of Origin and agreements on micro, small, and medium enterprises, entrepreneurship, and crafts to lower cross-border procedural barriers. On the multilateral front, both nations reaffirmed coordination under the World Trade Organization, G20, and BRICS frameworks. India recognised Brazil's participation in the Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership 2030 and the GVC Action Plan 2026-2030, while Brazil acknowledged Indian initiatives such as the BRICS Startup Knowledge Hub and the BRICS Business Incubator. Alongside official negotiations, an India-Brazil High Level Business Reception took place in Brasilia. Agrawal led an Indian business delegation of more than 25 corporate entities, including representatives from Kirloskar Group, UPL, and Aditya Birla Group, to evaluate joint ventures in critical minerals, renewable energy, digital services, logistics, and advanced manufacturing. Both sides also welcomed the establishment of the ApexBrasil office in New Delhi to facilitate direct investment inflows. Brazil is India's largest trade partner in the Latin America region, with bilateral trade of USD 15.21 billion in 2025. Daily Excelsior 04:51 AM Aug 31, 2026 IST Journalists from Ahmedabad being briefed about the historical significance of Amar Mahal in Jammu on Sunday. Excelsior Correspondent JAMMU, Aug 30: A 10-member media delegation from Ahmedabad arrived in Jammu today for a four-day press tour organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) to familiarise journalists with the region's cultural heritage, developmental initiatives and major infrastructure projects. The delegation was received at Jammu Airport by PIB officials. During the first day of the tour, the journalists visited the historic Amar Mahal Palace, where they were taken on a guided tour and briefed about its historical and cultural significance. The delegation also visited the Raghunath Temple. Advertisement During the visit, the delegation is scheduled to tour several important institutions and development projects across the Jammu division. These include IIT Jammu and major infrastructure projects of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), including the Delhi-Amritsar-Katra Expressway. The team is also scheduled to visit the Chenab Rail Bridge, Salal Hydroelectric Project in Reasi district and Biotech Park in Kathua, besides other important projects. The press tour is aimed at providing the participating journalists with first-hand information about the development and infrastructure initiatives being undertaken in the region, along with an opportunity to explore Jammu's rich cultural heritage. The delegation will also interact with officials and stakeholders during the tour. national_raw_news.title: Department of Consumer Affairs Notifies Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 - PIB
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution Department of Consumer Affairs Notifies Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 Rules to establish Indian Standard Time as common time reference across the country Rules to come into force after 180 days Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 11:27AM by PIB Delhi The Department of Consumer Affairs has notified the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 on 27 August 2026 . The Rules will come into force 180 days from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette . The Rules provide for Indian Standard Time (IST) as the common time reference across the country for legal, administrative, commercial and other official purposes. The 180-day period will allow Government departments, businesses, institutions and other organisations to make the required changes to their systems before the Rules come into force. The need for a common time reference has increased with the growing use of digital and technology-based systems. Banking and digital payments, telecommunications, railways, power systems, computer networks and government records depend on accurate time and time stamps. Differences between time sources can affect the coordination and recording of such activities. The Rules are aimed at ensuring that important systems across the country use accurate and consistent Indian Standard Time . The common time reference will support: accurate time-stamping of banking and digital payment transactions ; coordination of railways, airports and other transport systems ; reliable operation of telecommunication and internet networks ; accurate time-keeping in power systems ; maintenance of government and legal records ; and coordination of emergency and other time-sensitive services . Use of Indian Timing Sources The Government is developing infrastructure to disseminate accurate Indian Standard Time across the country through Indian institutions and Legal Metrology laboratories . The Rules also provide for the use of NavIC, India's satellite navigation system , and other approved Indian timing sources for reliable and secure time dissemination. At present, several systems use foreign satellite-based time sources. The development of an Indian time dissemination infrastructure will provide additional options for critical systems and reduce dependence on external time sources. White Rabbit Technology Demonstration As part of the ‘One Nation, One Time’ initiative, a White Rabbit Technology-based Indian Standard Time Dissemination Demonstration Network was commissioned at the Regional Reference Standard Laboratory (RRSL), Bengaluru, in July 2026 . The system has demonstrated the dissemination of Indian Standard Time for sectors including banking, telecommunications, power, transportation and digital governance . The Department has also demonstrated secure dissemination of IST between RRSL Bengaluru and NSE Chennai , in collaboration with CSIR-NPL, ISRO, SEBI, NSE, BSNL and other stakeholders . The 180-day period before commencement of the Rules will provide stakeholders time to review their existing systems, undertake necessary technical changes and prepare for implementation.The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 will provide a common Indian Standard Time reference for time-dependent systems and official purposes across the country . *** RT/ SB / ARC (Release ID: 2304613) Visitor Counter : 4586 Read this release in:...
